$comment: Every site this monitor watches, with what a healthy response looks like
for each. Health is defined per site rather than globally because these
differ wildly: the APIs answer 404 at / and that is correct, whisper
redirects to /login, and BiteBox once served a 200 while its database was
down. A single 'is it 200?' rule would be wrong for most of these.
expectStatus - any of these codes counts as up.
expectText   - this must appear in the body. This is the part that catches
a page that loads but is broken; without it, an error page
returned with a 200 looks perfectly healthy.
rejectText   - if this appears, the site is down even on a 200.
followRedirects - for sites whose root legitimately redirects.

targets.name: bitebox
targets.expectText: Good food, brought to your door
targets.note: Food delivery app. expectText is rendered from Postgres, so this also proves the database is reachable.

targets.name: whisper
targets.note: Root 307s to /login, which is correct behaviour, so redirects are followed.

targets.name: voltix-api
targets.note: An API with no root route. The 404 IS the healthy answer - it proves the app is running and routing. A plain status check would report this down forever.

targets.name: portfolio-backend
targets.note: Express default for an unmatched route, which means Express is alive.
